long_biography.plain_text:
At seventeen, Theocharakis joined the Piraeus automotive business that his father, Nicholas, had established in 1924. He later helped secure Nissan's first European distributorship and took charge of the family group after his brother Ioannis died. Under his leadership, the business moved beyond cars and tyres into industries including shipping, construction, finance and healthcare.

Painting developed in parallel rather than after business. While studying law in Athens, Theocharakis spent five years learning from Spyros Papaloukas, then first exhibited in Moscow and Athens in 1957. Landscapes remained the focus of his oils and watercolours across decades of exhibitions. His work is held by Greece's National Gallery and other public collections, making artistic practice a sustained second profession rather than a ceremonial family interest.

uncertainties.detail: Greek sources use Βασίλης or the formal Βασίλειος, while English sources use Vassilis, Vasilis, Vassilios or Basil. Piraeus, 1930, law studies, the Theocharakis family group, painting and the named foundation converge on one person. A younger Vassilis Theocharakis who teaches marketing at Cranfield is excluded.

Nicholas Theocharakis founded the underlying automotive business in 1924. Vassilis joined it as the founder's son and later expanded and diversified the group, so inherited and expanded with an Operator relationship is more precise than Founder.

The current group site presents Panagiotis Theocharakis as vice-president and managing director, while a 2024 regulatory biography still identifies Vassilios Theocharakis as president and chief executive. The proposed title uses the durable chairman formulation; current foundation presidency is independently documented in 2026.

The group has automotive, shipping, construction and other interests, but its official history and current public identity continue to centre on Nissan and automotive distribution. Public sources do not provide a comparable valuation of each branch, so Automotive is retained with lower confidence than wealth origin.
